items.title: Like A Sumo
items.summary: I'm getting kinda fat. There I said it. Dad bod. My…
items.content_html:
I'm getting kinda fat.

There I said it.

Dad bod.

My older (younger) body liked nay loved the iron.

This newer (oldish) body don't.

It just don't.

It likes aluminum.

Lined bags.

Filled with Doritos.

Awful.

Just awful.

The older, younger, body let me down.

Sure, it was fast(ish).

Strong(ish).

But it broke down.

Left me by the side of the road.

Almost totaled.

Almost.

Sure, it could lift more than 225 over my head for reps (seated military) but that strength means nothing if you deed.

If you deed.

Now I lift aluminum cans.

Much lighter weights.

More reps.

Counter to lips.

Over and over.

Not the healthiest way to do things.

It's just coke zero. No beers.

But I'm here to do things.

Not deed.

And the best part of having this new, old(ish), fattish body is that it comes with this brain, man.

This brain thinks differently.

These eyes see with different lenses.

And this heart feels fuller, somehow.

Maybe that's where all the muscle went.

So thankful.

So grateful.

So blessed.

To be getting fat.

Insane.

"Fat boy on a diet.

Don't try it."

items.title: Booth Or Tablet
items.summary: If I was in the mood to mentor, I'd pick a…
items.content_html:
If I was in the mood to mentor, I'd pick a booth.

Huh?

Like say you called me up.

How the heck they get this number?

I don't answer.

I don't see it.

You leave voicemail.

I get to it eventually.

We set up a lunch.

I pick a booth.

That's where I like to mentor.

A booth.

Tables aren't it.

I'm a booth guy.

Can't mentor at a table.

Or a tablet.

📱

Maybe you can.

Of course, I don't mentor.

I'm retired.

Ohhh, that's why.

I don't like that word.

So let's call me secluded.

I'm secluded.

Where was I?

Oh, yes, mentorsheet.

When I did, I notice looking back that they were all in booths.

Mostly in booths.

Might have been a table once or twice.

I'm not a guy who stands up and talks to a crowd and owns the room.

I don't do that.

I'm a guy who booths.

I can own a booth.

Or used to.

A guy who owned booths.

Booth owner.

I think they call it introverted.

But I'm just outroverted.

🍽

So, why am I sitting here?

Did you order apps?

Where's my two coke zeros?

You put anything in this?

Smells funny.

Get a pitcher of zero.

Work on that.

I gotta use the can.

This man walking around here like he's Ray Kroc.

items.content_html: "Never treat the highly likely as certain and the highly unlikely as impossible."

items.title: Kinda Mean
items.summary: Part of the deal that comes with being an old(ish) curmudgeon…
items.content_html:
Part of the deal that comes with being an old(ish) curmudgeon is you gotta be mad.

It's kinda crucial to the whole gimmick.

Outraged.

Cantankerous.

Great word.

So what do you make of an old(ish) curmudgeon who's just having the time of his life?

Grinning through the madness.

The only way to go.

There's an old line that I like to quote.

About how New Yorkers are not nice but they are kind.

And how Californians are nice but they are not kind.

And the example I heard recently was if you had something in your teeth.

That a New Yorker would say, "Hey fool, you got something in your teeth."

Not nice, but kind.

Whereas the Californian would just let you walk around with it.

And how the line in that song that's really just a commencement speech talks about living in New York City once but to leave before it makes you hard.

And the same for Northern California but leaving before it makes you soft.

But the teeth thing isn't really right.

It's more like this.

The kind not nice thing.

Let's move away from oral hygiene.

There's an old movie with Will Smith.

Back when it was ok to like him.

He was chasing something, then.

He's homeless and trying to make a living with a young son.

The details aren't important.

But he's in the city.

And he's running to cross the street at lunch hour.

A car hits him.

Boom!

And the guy gets out and looks genuinely concerned for Will.

"Hey arsehole. Are you okay, arsehole?"

That's not nice but kind.

Although it's a movie.

Set in San Francisco.

So maybe it's a city thing.

Not a state.

But that's the difference.

The other way would be to be really nice to Will, getting his contact information so you could later sue him (hopefully well insured and/or net worth it) for the damage to your car, emotional distress, hospital bills, physical therapy, loss of consortium, etc.

Or to avoid same.

Nice, not kind.

See the difference?

It's like that line Southerners say.

"Bless your heart."

Can be a polite insult.

The city way to say that is "What the fook wrong with you?"

So I leave you with this:

Nice and kind are not the same.

Not even similar.

And the nicest people you will encounter may be the worst.

And the kindest may seem a little rough around the center.

This is exceptional, of course.

Most nice people are decent.

Likable.

Most kind people are obviously so.

Radiant.

And the other way, too.

But sometimes, just sometimes, the maddest dog in the kennel, is also the sweetest.

🐺

Oh, I wasn't referring to me.

I'm a dragon.

🐲

Are you okay?

I'm fine, fool.

Say, what's your name?

Are you judgment proof?

Next!!!

items.title: Angels On My Shoulders
items.summary: You don't need the new Mac Mini. Yes, I do. No,…
items.content_html:
You don't need the new Mac Mini.

Yes, I do.

No, you don't.

But.

You already have too much tech.

Well, I should.

I'm a tech influencer.

No, you are most certainly not.

So it turns out, I'm not a tech influencer.

Which is news to me.

I thought everybody watched my videos.

You don't make any videos.

Hit the like and subscribe, fam.

Do they have those for musings columns?

I want a big arse award mailed to me with a book logo made of platinum.

📓

Something to let me know I made it.

I'll put it next to my new Mac Mini.

M6!

M5 Pro is better!

Which is weird nomenclature but welcome to the way we do things, now.

📓🍎

Sweet.

items.title: Actualization
items.summary: I don't want you to get the wrong idea. I want…
items.content_html:
I don't want you to get the wrong idea.

I want you to get the right idea.

So which ones do you get?

I'm hoping the latter.

But as we all know, ideas are everywhere.

Free and contagious.

Wrong idea gets you, whooo boy.

It keels ya.

But a right one.

A right one.

Goes the other way.

It births ya.

Now a good idea only gets you so far.

You need to act upon the idea.

To turn it from thought into thing.

Iterating on the thing over and over until it gets closer to perfection, or at least, its peak.

Good enough.

I would call it Actualization, but hey, I already did.

It's kinda the point.

The whole point.

To all of this.

[Hands waving in random, dramatic, circles.]

Meh.

Just an idea.

What do I know?

💭 to ♾ to ⏏️

items.title: Asian Raisins
items.summary: I don't feel old. I mean, I sorta do. Oldish. Energy…
items.content_html:
I don't feel old.

I mean, I sorta do.

Oldish.

Energy on low.

Vibes on high.

Me in the middle.

Just happy to be here.

But I look in the mirror and I can still see youngish me.

Signs of him.

Particularly since I shaved the locks off.

The lion's mane, mane.

I was looking like Steven Seagal.

Which, all due respect to the Glimmer Man, I wasn't really going for.

Asian don't raisin.

Did I make that up?

I don't want to search if I did.

So let's just say I did.

Taking credit, whether or not it's due.

Unless you really old, then you sorta look like a raisin.

If you're Asian.

And lucky enough to ferment.

Some lady turned 117 recently.

Not Asian, but still quite raisiny.

To dried grapes.

Aging like fine wine.

🍇

items.title: Power En Masse
items.summary: What do you make of the Richest Man in the World…
items.content_html:
What do you make of the Richest Man in the World telling you that money won't exist in ten years?

Or at least not matter.

Only power and mass will.

Sure, he might mean it.

I don't know what that means.

But also seems like something only the richest in the world would say.

So you don't get too angry.

Too riled up.

Too out of sorts.

At the title.

At the numbers.

At the magnitude.

Nothing to see here folks.

It's only money, guys.

Chill.

It won't matter soon.

It won't even exist.

Soon(ish).

Trust.

The city in me says prove it.

Give up some.

Right now.

Money.

Mouth.

Is.

And maybe they are.

I don't know.

Won't matter soon, right?

But it would matter now.

To a lot of folks.

A lot of good folks.

If they truly believed that, wouldn't they put it to help right now while it still did?

While it still could?

Is that what they're doing?

Why hoard it, if they truly believed it wouldn't matter soon?

As a hedge?

Something I'm missing?

Money ain't going nowhere.

If we call it a sock, it'll still be money.

I think we're saying the same thing, here.

I'm not hating vehemently disliking.

I don't do that.

I am simply making an observation.

A simple observation.

🔭

Just my two socks.

🧦🧦

items.title: Lions, Mane, Lions
items.summary: You know what they call me? Alex "All Day" Chung. No…
items.content_html:
You know what they call me?

Alex "All Day" Chung.

No one has ever called you that in your entire life.

Well, I call myself that.

That's true.

I suppose I've been called and called myself many things.

So many.

Most deserved.

But some uncalled for.

Just not called for at all.

I've been called absurd a lot lately.

And I dig it.

It's what I've been going for.

Reach for the stars, All Day.

As I've said before, though, you never go full absurd.

Just enough absurd.

Within reason.

Goldilocks absurd.

But it's time, I think, to put absurdity to bed.

At least, full(ish) absurdity.

With a bowl of porridge.

Night night.

So, not that you care, but my ebony locks are gone, baby.

Or at least on the floor.

Looks like there's a mullet wig laying there (we have several).

Back to "Old Daddy" as my babies called it.

Old(ish) Daddy.

Feels good.

Head swivels.

Hair don't follow, it stays tight, with me.

No delays.

I'll miss tossing it up with my hand, but alas, life's a trade.

My head, already quite prodigious, feels light(ish).

A heavy feather.

But still a feather.

I could go on all day.

All Day!!!

items.title: Sometimes 4 GB > 1 TB
items.summary: Today, I want to talk about thumb drives. You know, usb…
items.content_html:
Today, I want to talk about thumb drives.

You know, usb drives.

Flash drives.

The little rectangles.

Now I got me some fancy ones.

1TB.

512s.

Got 'em before the price jack.

Which I count as a huge win for some reason.

Got 'em.

But here's the thing.

They kinda sook.

Slow.

Temperamental.

Unreliable.

They look cool.

Fancy.

Fidgety.

I flip one way it's usb a, I flip the other and it's usb c!

But they sook.

Now, lately I've been reaching for a 4 gb dinosaur I've had for 20 years.

Why?

Because it works every friggin' time.

Because it's fast.

In. Out. In. Out.

Bada bing.

Bada boom.

Done.

Of course, the storage could be an issue but it's not for me.

Just a way to go from A to B to C.

It's not all function, either.

It's pretty, too.

Made of titanium.

Looks brand new.

Apparently, the way they make thumb drives today means they won't last nearly as long as these old ones.

Ain't that something?

We're very much in a stage where old tech can be better than what's new.

At least in some ways.

Like an old V8 engine.

Sheety gas mileage.

But it'll go forever.

Like my 4 gb thumb drive.

And maybe it's because I'm old(ish).

A forward seeing but nostalgic some gun.

Or maybe, just maybe, we really used to do it better.

When you pay up, you expect things to work at a higher commensurate level.

We all know that just ain't always so.

To old(ish) tech.

Still running like new.

Heaven yeah.

But all that can change.

In a flash.

👍
